symptom: `describe entity Probe.Child` printed `create or modify persistent entity Probe.Child extends Probe.Base (` when Probe.Base is non-persistent; check and exec were clean, and the same wrong flag reached the catalog's EntityType, mermaid/ELK diagrams, the microflow builder's entityPersistable map, and `alter entities in Probe add attribute … where persistent`, which added the attribute to the non-persistent Probe.Child too. The virtual System module had it too: System.HttpRequest, HttpResponse and SoapFault read persistent although HttpMessage and Error are not.
cause: A specialization's MaybeGeneralization is a DomainModels$Generalization, which has no Persistable property — the flag lives only on the root's NoGeneralization. entityFromGen initialised Persistable to true and only the NoGeneralization arm overwrote it, so a specialization always read the default; the System meta table likewise carried a meaningless `Persistable: true` on its specializations.
file: `mdl/backend/modelsdk/domainmodel.go` (`resolveInheritedPersistability`, called by ListDomainModels / GetDomainModel / GetDomainModelByID over every stored domain model plus the System entities); `domainmodel_carry.go` (`entityUnchanged` takes the statement's value for a specialization)
insight: A property Mendix stores on only one end of a chain is a READ of the chain, not a field of the element — entityFromGen sees one entity and cannot answer it, so the resolution belongs in the domain-model reads, which already decode every module. Resolve it there and every consumer (describe, the bulk `where persistent` filter, catalog, diagrams) is fixed at once; patching cmd_entities_describe.go alone would have left four. The trap on the way: once reads return the resolved value, any 'is this unchanged?' comparison against entityFromGen's raw default calls every specialization of a non-persistent entity changed and rebuilds it on each UpdateDomainModel — treat the inherited value like the 11+ view OQL, as not the element's content. The CLI round trip did not show that churn (write elision caught it), so it needs a unit test on entityUnchanged with a root-entity control.
